correctness.rationale: Each nonfixed update decreases the integer sum, so T_n is at most 2n and a fixed state is absorbing. The cited one-site densities give the exact drop (t+15)/(81·3^t); a cone with 2t+3 distinct sites transfers this drop to the ring, giving the claimed Markov bound for T_n>t. The two zero endpoints of 0·2^a·1^b·0 are permanent. For a−1 updates the two descending boundaries move together, and for b−1 more updates the ones erode, forcing a change into time a+b−2. There are t−1 splits. At n≥2(t+4), interior overlaps are incompatible, only the two shared-endpoint offsets can add covariance, and disjoint windows are independent. This gives Var Z≤EZ+2n(t−1)^2·3^(−2(t+4)+1) and the stated lower tail. The two tails at the logarithmic center are geometric; above the valid cone range use the deterministic horizon, and below half log_3 n use monotonicity. Summing gives bounded absolute mean deviation, not just tightness. Independent bounded replay: checks/replay_certificates.py (fixation); finite checks supplement the literature input and analytic proof.
residual_risks: The all-depth one-site density identity is imported from the 2015 paper; its general FSM derivation is not reproduced, and finite enumeration is not its proof.
No limiting lattice law or other initial distribution is established.
